g.text: Ours: what Orchestra owns and runs
Interface: where work crosses, and my outbox

g.title: Someone asks me for a simple task; more asks when requesters trust me to deliver. — crosses: slack/jira in
Confidence fades on its own, faster while bugs are open, and faster when asks sit in my backlog.
research + ticket — crosses: read: jira, docs, slack, code
approve ticket — crosses: jira write (via outbox)
An implementation attempt with tests. Slower where the debt is high.
Failures and late findings leave lessons, and successes leave patterns worth keeping, unless the backlog is long and nobody stops to write them down.
The agents turn lessons into policies, docs, skills and tools for themselves.
About six weeks' half-life, faster when much is landing in the area.
Every landing adds some debt; flawed ones add more; a good playbook adds less.
Agents pay debt down when they have time; under load this is the first thing squeezed.
Company checks and the AI reviewer catch about 40% of flaws.
Company checks and the AI reviewer catch about 40% of flaws.
crosses: read: threads; github push; replies via outbox
Approved with the flaw still in it; it lands, and surfaces later.
crosses: read: SAIL logs; github label
Trust erodes slowly on its own, and sharply when flaws are found late or bugs appear.
How much other teams expect me to deliver. It brings asks, grows with landings, falls with bugs.
Researched and written up; waiting for my approval.
Ready for an implementation attempt: new tickets, diagnosed failures, bugs coming back.
An attempt finished; its outcome is decided by the playbook and the debt.
Looks done, tests pass, but has a defect nobody has seen yet.
Visibly failed attempts, flaws I caught, and flaws reviewers caught: to be diagnosed.
Policies, docs, skills and tools the agents use for this class of task, written by the agents from lessons.
Shortcuts in the code the agents work in.
Decides how much of the agents' work I check myself.
Change requests on sound PRs: style, naming, small asks. A fix round, not a flaw.
A real flaw found by company checks or reviewers. It costs trust and teaches a lesson.
Landed in about the last two weeks: the code churn that ages the playbook, and the evidence that builds trust and reputation.
Landed and out of the recent window.
